note: Zapin (gambus lute and marwas drums, from Arab-Hadhrami roots) and joget (quick violin-led couple dance) are two Malay social dances usually heard side by side; dance-music albums label each track with its rhythm. Field recordings from Riau and Sumatra sit next to Malaysian dance orchestras and pop singers who kept the forms alive.

size.basis: No source counts recordings. Discogs text search finds 220 hits for zapin and 1359 for joget (the latter includes many dangdut and pop records named after the dance). From 1949 to the 1980s Malaysian and Singapore labels issued many joget singles and EPs and joget compilations of 14 singers (EMI Joget Pilihan, 1982); dance-music LPs (1974, 1978, 1983, 1990) label each track zapin, joget or inang. Indonesian Melayu zapin is mostly on local cassettes: Folkways notes no recordings from Sumatra or Riau were published outside Indonesia before its 1996 volume. An insider list would be about 40: the standard dance tunes (Serampang Laut, Hitam Manis, Kamarulzaman, Gambus Palembang, Lancang Kuning and similar) in a few versions each.
